claim: PBMCs purified using gradient centrifugation are a major source of clinically relevant cells for the study of human immune health and disease.
source: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) purified using gradient centrifugation are a major source of clinically relevant cells for the study of human immune health and disease (Böyum, 1968).
evidence: Supported by citation to Böyum, 1968

claim: PBMCs are a complex, heterogeneous mixture of cell types derived from common stem cell progenitors.
source: Like most other human tissues, PBMCs are a complex, heterogeneous mixture of cell types derived from common stem cell progenitors (Laurenti and Göttgens, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Laurenti and Göttgens, 2018

claim: The genome is mostly invariant between different PBMC cell types.
source: Despite the genome being mostly invariant between different PBMC cell types, each immune cell type performs an important and distinct function.
evidence: Based on established biological knowledge

claim: Each immune cell type performs an important and distinct function.
source: Despite the genome being mostly invariant between different PBMC cell types, each immune cell type performs an important and distinct function.
evidence: Based on established biological knowledge

claim: Understanding the genomic regulatory landscape that controls lineage specification, cellular maturation, activation state, and functional diversity is key to understanding the immune system in both health and disease.
source: Understanding the genomic regulatory landscape that controls lineage specification, cellular maturation, activation state, and functional diversity in response to intra- and extracellular signals is key to understanding the immune system in both health and disease (Satpathy et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2020; Zheng et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Satpathy et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2020; Zheng et al., 2020

claim: Recent improvements in single-cell genomic methods have enabled profiling of the regulatory chromatin landscape of complex cell-type mixtures.
source: Recent improvements in single-cell genomic methods have enabled profiling of the regulatory chromatin landscape of complex cell-type mixtures.
evidence: Based on established knowledge in the field

claim: Droplet-based single-nucleus or single-cell assays for transposase-accessible chromatin allow profiling of open chromatin at single-cell resolution.
source: In particular, droplet-based single-nucleus or single-cell assays for transposase-accessible chromatin (snATAC-seq, scATAC-seq, dscATAC-seq, mtscATAC-seq) allow profiling of open chromatin at single-cell resolution (Buenrostro et al., 2015; Lareau et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Buenrostro et al., 2015; Lareau et al., 2019

claim: New methods have combined scATAC-seq with simultaneous measurement of nuclear mRNAs.
source: Promising new methods have combined scATAC-seq with simultaneous measurement of nuclear mRNAs (e.g., sci-CAR, Cao et al., 2018; SNARE-seq, Chen et al., 2019; SHARE-seq, Ma et al., 2020) or in combination with cell surface epitopes (ASAP-seq, Mimitou et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Cao et al., 2018; Chen et al., 2019; Ma et al., 2020

claim: New methods have combined scATAC-seq with cell surface epitopes.
source: Promising new methods have combined scATAC-seq with simultaneous measurement of nuclear mRNAs (e.g., sci-CAR, Cao et al., 2018; SNARE-seq, Chen et al., 2019; SHARE-seq, Ma et al., 2020) or in combination with cell surface epitopes (ASAP-seq, Mimitou et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Mimitou et al., 2020

claim: A unifying approach for all three modalities (ATAC, RNA, and epitopes) that can be applied to highly specified functional immune cell types has yet to emerge.
source: However, a unifying approach for all three modalities that can be applied to highly specified functional immune cell types has yet to emerge in the landscape of single-cell methods.
evidence: Based on assessment of the current state of the field

claim: Intact, permeabilized cells perform extremely well for scATAC-seq, exceeding conventional scATAC-seq on nuclei by some measures.
source: We found that intact, permeabilized cells perform extremely well for scATAC-seq, exceeding conventional scATAC-seq on nuclei by some measures (Figure 1b).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1b

claim: ICICLE-seq is a new protocol to measure both surface protein abundance and chromatin accessibility.
source: This insight enables a new protocol analogous to Cellular Indexing of Transcriptomes and Epitopes (CITE-seq; Stoeckius et al., 2017) to measure both surface protein abundance and chromatin accessibility: integrated cellular indexing of chromatin landscape and epitopes (ICICLE-seq, Figures 1a and 3).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figures 1a and 3, and citation to Stoeckius et al., 2017

claim: TEA-seq enables simultaneous measurement of mRNA, protein, and DNA from thousands of single cells.
source: Finally, we demonstrate that our optimized permeable cell approach can be combined with a droplet-based multiomics platform to enable the simultaneous measurement of three different molecular compartments of the cell: mRNA (by scRNA-seq), protein (using oligo-tagged antibodies), and DNA (by scATAC-seq), which we term TEA-seq after Transcription, Epitopes, and Accessibility (Figure 4).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4

claim: snATAC-seq libraries prepared from nuclei contained many more reads originating from nucleosomal DNA fragments than scATAC-seq libraries from permeabilized cells.
source: scATAC-seq libraries prepared from nuclei contained many more reads originating from nucleosomal DNA fragments (Figure 1b, lower panels), and non-cell barcodes from nuclei (gray lines) contained more of these fragments than cell barcodes.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1b, lower panels

claim: Libraries from permeabilized cells consisted almost entirely of short fragments.
source: Libraries from permeabilized cells consisted almost entirely of short fragments, suggesting that permeabilization under isotonic conditions did not loosen or release native chromatin structure at the time of tagmentation (Figure 1b, lower panels).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1b, lower panels

claim: Permeabilization under isotonic conditions did not loosen or release native chromatin structure at the time of tagmentation.
source: Libraries from permeabilized cells consisted almost entirely of short fragments, suggesting that permeabilization under isotonic conditions did not loosen or release native chromatin structure at the time of tagmentation (Figure 1b, lower panels).
evidence: Inferred from fragment length data shown in Figure 1b

claim: Hypotonic lysis leads to alteration of chromatin structure.
source: In agreement with in vitro experiments studying the effects of low salt on nucleosomal arrays (Allahverdi et al., 2015), this further suggests that hypotonic lysis leads to alteration of chromatin structure, raising the possibility of artifactual measurements of accessibility in nuclei-based ATAC-seq.
evidence: Supported by citation to Allahverdi et al., 2015 and inference from data

claim: The signal at TSS was retained in permeabilized cells.
source: The signal at TSS was retained in permeabilized cells, but positions flanking the TSS (occupied by neighboring nucleosomes) had reduced signal compared to isolated nuclei (examined in detail in Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1c and Figure 1—figure supplement 6

claim: At CTCF motifs, nearly identical patterns of accessibility were observed in both nuclei and permeabilized cells.
source: At CTCF motifs, we observed nearly identical patterns of accessibility in both nuclei and permeabilized cells, suggesting that scATAC-seq signal at regulatory TFBS is retained in permeabilized cells.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1d

claim: scATAC-seq signal at regulatory TFBS is retained in permeabilized cells.
source: At CTCF motifs, we observed nearly identical patterns of accessibility in both nuclei and permeabilized cells, suggesting that scATAC-seq signal at regulatory TFBS is retained in permeabilized cells.
evidence: Inferred from CTCF motif data shown in Figure 1d

claim: Permeabilized intact cells obtained by FACS had the highest FRIP and FRITSS scores.
source: Overall, permeabilized intact cells obtained by FACS had the highest FRIP and FRITSS scores, fewest non-cell barcodes, and greatest cell capture efficiency with only a modest increase in mitochondrial reads (Table 1, Figure 1e, f).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Table 1, Figure 1e, f

claim: Removal of neutrophils greatly improved the ability to separate various cell types in UMAP projections of both nuclei and cells.
source: Removal of neutrophils greatly improved the ability to separate various cell types in uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) projections of both nuclei and cells (Figure 2a, b).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2a, b

claim: Removal of neutrophils improved label transfer scores.
source: Using these tools, removal of neutrophils improved label transfer scores, and permeabilized cells yielded more cells with high label transfer scores than nuclei-based approaches (Figure 2b, c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2b, c

claim: Permeabilized cells yielded more cells with high label transfer scores than nuclei-based approaches.
source: Using these tools, removal of neutrophils improved label transfer scores, and permeabilized cells yielded more cells with high label transfer scores than nuclei-based approaches (Figure 2b, c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2b, c

claim: Permeabilized cells provided labels most similar to the cell-type proportions identified by flow cytometry.
source: In addition, permeabilized cells provided labels most similar to the cell-type proportions identified by flow cytometry (Figure 2d), with identification of CD8 effector cells only observed in scATAC-seq with permeabilized cells.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2d

claim: CD8 effector cells were only identified in scATAC-seq with permeabilized cells.
source: In addition, permeabilized cells provided labels most similar to the cell-type proportions identified by flow cytometry (Figure 2d), with identification of CD8 effector cells only observed in scATAC-seq with permeabilized cells.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2d

claim: All methods yielded fewer CD16+ monocytes than observed by flow cytometry.
source: All methods yielded fewer CD16+ monocytes than observed by flow cytometry, suggesting that CD16+ monocytes may be lost during scATAC-seq using either nuclei or permeabilized cells, or that label transfer methods were not conducive to identifying this cell type (Figure 2d).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2d

claim: Many more differentially accessible sites were found in both cells and nuclei after removal of neutrophils.
source: We found many more differentially accessible sites in both cells and nuclei after removal of neutrophils.
evidence: Supported by differential accessibility analysis

claim: Without neutrophil removal, significantly enriched motifs could not be identified in B cells and NK cells.
source: Without neutrophil removal (nuclei unsorted, top panel), we were unable to identify significantly enriched motifs in B cells and NK cells that were readily apparent in data from clean nuclei or permeabilized cells (bottom two panels).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2b

claim: Neutrophil removal and the use of permeabilized cells allow for identification of specific cell types and TFBS motifs involved in regulation of gene expression.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that neutrophil removal and the use of permeabilized cells allow for identification of specific cell types and TFBS motifs that are involved in regulation of gene expression.
evidence: Inferred from the combined results of cell type identification and motif enrichment analyses

claim: 10,227 single cells with both scATAC-seq and ADT data were obtained from three ICICLE-seq capture wells.
source: We performed ICICLE-seq on a leukapheresis-purified PBMC sample using a 46-antibody panel (Supplementary file 6) and were able to obtain 10,227 single cells with both scATAC-seq and ADT data from three capture wells that passed adjusted QC criteria: >500 unique ATAC fragments (median = 761), FRIP >0.65 (median = 0.725).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from ICICLE-seq

claim: Cells passing ATAC QC in ICICLE-seq had a median of 3871 ADT UMIs per cell.
source: Cells passing ATAC QC had a median of 3871 ADT unique molecule indexes (UMIs) per cell (Figure 3—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2b

claim: UMAP projection and ATAC label transfer on ICICLE-seq data had resolution similar to scATAC-seq on intact permeabilized cells after dead cell and debris removal.
source: UMAP projection and ATAC label transfer on ICICLE-seq data had resolution similar to scATAC-seq on intact permeabilized cells after dead cell and debris removal (Figure 3b).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3b

claim: The data quality of ICICLE-seq was limited by the poly-A-based capture method and the single-end readout of transposed fragments.
source: However, the data quality was limited by the poly-A-based capture method and the single-end readout of transposed fragments.
evidence: Based on assessment of technical limitations

claim: ICICLE-seq demonstrated that permeabilized cells enabled simultaneous capture of chromatin accessibility in the nucleus and high-quality cell surface epitope quantification.
source: Nonetheless, the ICICLE-seq results demonstrated that permeabilized cells enabled simultaneous capture of chromatin accessibility in the nucleus and high-quality cell surface epitope quantification.
evidence: Inferred from ICICLE-seq results

claim: ICICLE-seq allowed identification of cell-type-specific clusters based on clear association of cell-type-specific markers with clusters.
source: We were able to leverage the additional ADT data to cluster and identify cell types based on their cell surface antigens (Figure 3c) UMAP based on ADT data, and Jaccard–Louvain clustering allowed identification of cell-type-specific clusters (Figure 3d) based on clear association of cell-type-specific markers with clusters (Figure 3e, Figure 3—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3c, d, e, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2c

claim: ICICLE-seq provided a key proof of principle for directly linked capture of functional cell types and chromatin accessibility.
source: Thus, ICICLE-seq provided a key proof of principle for directly linked capture of functional cell types and chromatin accessibility.
evidence: Inferred from ICICLE-seq results

claim: 29,264 cell barcodes passed QC criteria for TEA-seq.
source: After initial data processing for cells loaded into four wells, we identified 29,264 cell barcodes that passed the QC criteria for scATAC-seq described above and had >2,500 unique ATAC-seq fragments (median = 8762 unique ATAC fragments, Figure 4b, d) and had >500 genes detected by scRNA-seq (median = 2399 RNA UMIs; median = 1,249 genes detected, Figure 4b), and >500 ADT UMIs (median = 1171 ADT UMIs, Figure 4c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4b, c, d

claim: TEA-seq cells had a median of 8762 unique ATAC fragments.
source: After initial data processing for cells loaded into four wells, we identified 29,264 cell barcodes that passed the QC criteria for scATAC-seq described above and had >2,500 unique ATAC-seq fragments (median = 8762 unique ATAC fragments, Figure 4b, d) and had >500 genes detected by scRNA-seq (median = 2399 RNA UMIs; median = 1,249 genes detected, Figure 4b), and >500 ADT UMIs (median = 1171 ADT UMIs, Figure 4c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4b, d

claim: TEA-seq cells had a median of 2399 RNA UMIs.
source: After initial data processing for cells loaded into four wells, we identified 29,264 cell barcodes that passed the QC criteria for scATAC-seq described above and had >2,500 unique ATAC-seq fragments (median = 8762 unique ATAC fragments, Figure 4b, d) and had >500 genes detected by scRNA-seq (median = 2399 RNA UMIs; median = 1,249 genes detected, Figure 4b), and >500 ADT UMIs (median = 1171 ADT UMIs, Figure 4c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4b

claim: TEA-seq cells had a median of 1,249 genes detected.
source: After initial data processing for cells loaded into four wells, we identified 29,264 cell barcodes that passed the QC criteria for scATAC-seq described above and had >2,500 unique ATAC-seq fragments (median = 8762 unique ATAC fragments, Figure 4b, d) and had >500 genes detected by scRNA-seq (median = 2399 RNA UMIs; median = 1,249 genes detected, Figure 4b), and >500 ADT UMIs (median = 1171 ADT UMIs, Figure 4c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4b

claim: TEA-seq cells had a median of 1171 ADT UMIs.
source: After initial data processing for cells loaded into four wells, we identified 29,264 cell barcodes that passed the QC criteria for scATAC-seq described above and had >2,500 unique ATAC-seq fragments (median = 8762 unique ATAC fragments, Figure 4b, d) and had >500 genes detected by scRNA-seq (median = 2399 RNA UMIs; median = 1,249 genes detected, Figure 4b), and >500 ADT UMIs (median = 1171 ADT UMIs, Figure 4c).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4c

claim: Marker expression is consistent across all three modalities for some markers, such as CD8A.
source: We found that marker expression is consistent across all three modalities for some markers, such as CD8A, though we found that consistency across all modalities is not a universal characteristic of functional markers (Figure 4—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2a

claim: Consistency across all modalities is not a universal characteristic of functional markers.
source: We found that marker expression is consistent across all three modalities for some markers, such as CD8A, though we found that consistency across all modalities is not a universal characteristic of functional markers (Figure 4—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2a

claim: The weights contributed by different modalities to the WNN analyses vary by cell type.
source: In agreement with observations by Hao and Hao et al. on two-modality data, the weights contributed by different modalities to the WNN analyses vary by cell type (Figure 4—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2b and citation to Hao et al.

claim: More sensitive protein abundance measures allowed detection of many additional correlated CRMs for some targets.
source: For some targets, however, more sensitive protein abundance measures allowed detection of many additional correlated CRMs.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of peak-to-gene and peak-to-protein correlations

claim: Peak-to-protein correlations identified many CRMs that were missed with peak-to-gene correlation alone for CCR2/CD192.
source: We present two examples – one of CCR2/CD192 (Figure 4g, h), a chemokine receptor expressed on monocytes (Tsou et al., 2007), and CD38 (Figure 4i, j), a glycoprotein expressed on the surface of multiple immune cell types (Ferrero and Malavasi, 2002), and a target of therapies for multiple myeloma (Dima et al., 2020; Sanchez et al., 2016). In both cases, peak-to-protein correlations identified many CRMs were missed with peak-to-gene correlation alone.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4g, h and citations

claim: Peak-to-protein correlations identified many CRMs that were missed with peak-to-gene correlation alone for CD38.
source: We present two examples – one of CCR2/CD192 (Figure 4g, h), a chemokine receptor expressed on monocytes (Tsou et al., 2007), and CD38 (Figure 4i, j), a glycoprotein expressed on the surface of multiple immune cell types (Ferrero and Malavasi, 2002), and a target of therapies for multiple myeloma (Dima et al., 2020; Sanchez et al., 2016). In both cases, peak-to-protein correlations identified many CRMs were missed with peak-to-gene correlation alone.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4i, j and citations

claim: CCR2 is a chemokine receptor expressed on monocytes.
source: We present two examples – one of CCR2/CD192 (Figure 4g, h), a chemokine receptor expressed on monocytes (Tsou et al., 2007), and CD38 (Figure 4i, j), a glycoprotein expressed on the surface of multiple immune cell types (Ferrero and Malavasi, 2002), and a target of therapies for multiple myeloma (Dima et al., 2020; Sanchez et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tsou et al., 2007

claim: CD38 is a glycoprotein expressed on the surface of multiple immune cell types.
source: We present two examples – one of CCR2/CD192 (Figure 4g, h), a chemokine receptor expressed on monocytes (Tsou et al., 2007), and CD38 (Figure 4i, j), a glycoprotein expressed on the surface of multiple immune cell types (Ferrero and Malavasi, 2002), and a target of therapies for multiple myeloma (Dima et al., 2020; Sanchez et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ferrero and Malavasi, 2002

claim: CD38 is a target of therapies for multiple myeloma.
source: We present two examples – one of CCR2/CD192 (Figure 4g, h), a chemokine receptor expressed on monocytes (Tsou et al., 2007), and CD38 (Figure 4i, j), a glycoprotein expressed on the surface of multiple immune cell types (Ferrero and Malavasi, 2002), and a target of therapies for multiple myeloma (Dima et al., 2020; Sanchez et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dima et al., 2020; Sanchez et al., 2016

claim: TEA-seq results appeared qualitatively similar to CITE-seq and scATAC-seq across assays.
source: In these direct comparisons, we found that TEA-seq results appeared qualitatively similar to CITE-seq and scATAC-seq across assays (Figure 4—figure supplement 4b, e, i).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4b, e, i

claim: The fraction of reads mapping to exons in TEA-seq was lower than that found in whole-cell CITE-seq data.
source: We found that the fraction of reads mapping to exons was lower than that found in whole-cell CITE-seq data, similar to that seen using a lysed-cell nuclei preparation (median fraction of reads with exonic mapping: TEA-seq, 51.8%, Nuclei Multiome, 52.2%; CITE-seq, 69.5% Figure 4—figure supplement 4c), suggesting the primary source of RNAs in TEA-seq is intron-containing nuclear transcripts.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4c

claim: The primary source of RNAs in TEA-seq is intron-containing nuclear transcripts.
source: We found that the fraction of reads mapping to exons was lower than that found in whole-cell CITE-seq data, similar to that seen using a lysed-cell nuclei preparation (median fraction of reads with exonic mapping: TEA-seq, 51.8%, Nuclei Multiome, 52.2%; CITE-seq, 69.5% Figure 4—figure supplement 4c), suggesting the primary source of RNAs in TEA-seq is intron-containing nuclear transcripts.
evidence: Inferred from exonic mapping data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4c

claim: Gene detection in TEA-seq was most like nuclei and lower in many cases than CITE-seq.
source: We found that gene detection was most like nuclei and lower in many cases than CITE-seq.
evidence: Supported by gene detection comparison data

claim: Ribosomal gene transcripts were particularly low in TEA-seq compared to CITE-seq.
source: One group of genes stands out as particularly low, originating from ribosomal gene transcripts (with gene symbols starting with RPL and RPS, highlighted in blue).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4d, g

claim: TEA-seq performed comparably to standalone permeabilized cell scATAC-seq or Multiome RNA + ATAC using permeabilized cells in scATAC-seq metrics.
source: In comparisons of scATAC-seq metrics, we found that TEA-seq performed comparably to standalone permeabilized cell scATAC-seq or Multiome RNA + ATAC using permeabilized cells, with higher FRIP than purified nuclei used for the same assay (Figure 4—figure supplement 4e, f).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4e, f

claim: TEA-seq had higher FRIP than purified nuclei used for the Multiome assay.
source: In comparisons of scATAC-seq metrics, we found that TEA-seq performed comparably to standalone permeabilized cell scATAC-seq or Multiome RNA + ATAC using permeabilized cells, with higher FRIP than purified nuclei used for the same assay (Figure 4—figure supplement 4e, f).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4e, f

claim: Antibody performance in TEA-seq varied by target.
source: Finally, in comparisons of protein detection by ADTs, we found that antibody performance in TEA-seq varied by target.
evidence: Supported by ADT distribution data

claim: Many bimodal distributions were retained in TEA-seq ADT data.
source: Many bimodal distributions were retained (e.g., CD4, CD8a, CD86), while some separations were less apparent (e.g., CD45RO and CD45RA; Figure 4—figure supplement 4h), resulting in reduced separation in UMAP analysis for some types (i.e., naïve vs. mature CD4 cells), though most major cell types were able to be separated (Figure 4—figure supplement 4i).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4h

claim: Some ADT separations were less apparent in TEA-seq compared to CITE-seq.
source: Many bimodal distributions were retained (e.g., CD4, CD8a, CD86), while some separations were less apparent (e.g., CD45RO and CD45RA; Figure 4—figure supplement 4h), resulting in reduced separation in UMAP analysis for some types (i.e., naïve vs. mature CD4 cells), though most major cell types were able to be separated (Figure 4—figure supplement 4i).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4h

claim: TEA-seq data is of high quality but may not always be the method of choice if a particular modality is of greatest interest.
source: Together, these results show that TEA-seq data is of high quality but may not always be the method of choice if a particular modality is of greatest interest to researchers.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of TEA-seq to standalone methods

claim: The strength of TEA-seq is its ability to measure all three aspects – transcription, epitopes, and accessibility – simultaneously on each cell.
source: The strength of TEA-seq is its ability to measure all three aspects – transcription, epitopes, and accessibility – simultaneously on each cell, enabling deeper insights into the connections between regulation, expression, and function as demonstrated in Figure 4.
evidence: Inferred from the trimodal nature of TEA-seq and data shown in Figure 4

claim: Multimodal data collection from permeabilized PBMCs will be of use to many researchers in the immunology field and beyond.
source: Multimodal data collection from permeabilized PBMCs will be of use to many researchers in the immunology field and beyond who seek to get the most high-quality data from precious clinical samples and to facilitate cross-datastream integration with flow cytometry.
evidence: Based on speculation about future utility

claim: Isotonic cell permeabilization allows the generation of scATAC-seq libraries with high quality as measured by FRIP and low nucleosomal content.
source: We found that isotonic cell permeabilization allows the generation of scATAC-seq libraries with high quality as measured by FRIP and low nucleosomal content, suggesting that chromatin state in the nucleus is unperturbed (Figure 1, Figure 2).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 1, Figure 2

claim: Chromatin state in the nucleus is unperturbed by isotonic cell permeabilization.
source: We found that isotonic cell permeabilization allows the generation of scATAC-seq libraries with high quality as measured by FRIP and low nucleosomal content, suggesting that chromatin state in the nucleus is unperturbed (Figure 1, Figure 2).
evidence: Inferred from FRIP and nucleosomal content data shown in Figure 1, Figure 2

claim: The use of permeabilized cells enables simultaneous interrogation of chromatin accessibility state in the nucleus and the functional state of cells based on their cell surface proteins at unprecedented scale.
source: While a previous study utilized FACS followed by scATAC on individually sorted cells (Pi-ATAC; Chen et al., 2018c), the use of permeabilized cells enables simultaneous interrogation of chromatin accessibility state in the nucleus and the functional state of cells based on their cell surface proteins (ICICLE-seq, Figure 3) together with mRNA (TEA-seq, Figure 4) at unprecedented scale for the first time.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3 and Figure 4, and citation to Chen et al., 2018c

claim: TEA-seq extends beyond SNARE-seq and SHARE-seq by taking advantage of 10x Genomics Single Cell Multiome sequencing reagents as a platform for nucleic acid capture.
source: Our methods utilize permeabilized cells to allow the addition of protein measurements that provide a direct link between high-quality scRNA-seq data and scATAC-seq data using truly paired methods extending beyond SNARE-seq (Chen et al., 2019) and SHARE-seq (Ma et al., 2020) by taking advantage of 10x Genomics Single Cell Multiome sequencing reagents as a platform for nucleic acid capture.
evidence: Supported by citations to Chen et al., 2019 and Ma et al., 2020

claim: The use of a droplet-based method allows multimodal measurements at a much higher scale by capturing thousands of single cells at a time.
source: The use of a droplet-based method allows multimodal measurements at a much higher scale by capturing thousands of single cells at a time.
evidence: Based on the nature of droplet-based methods

claim: The datasets generated by this study will be useful beyond researchers studying PBMC biology, including those seeking to develop new analytical tools.
source: We expect that the datasets generated by our study will be useful beyond researchers studying PBMC biology, including those seeking to develop new analytical tools to remove background noise from existing sn/scATAC-seq data (e.g., SCALE, Xiong et al., 2019, or scOpen, Li et al., 2019b) and tools to accurately identify links across modalities (e.g., AI-TAC, Tasaki et al., 2020).
evidence: Based on speculation about future utility, with citations to Xiong et al., 2019; Li et al., 2019b; Tasaki et al., 2020

claim: TEA-seq optimized for PBMCs will provide unprecedented biological insight into the molecular underpinnings of human immune health and disease.
source: As such, TEA-seq optimized for PBMCs will provide unprecedented biological insight into the molecular underpinnings of human immune health and disease.
evidence: Based on speculation about future utility

claim: The use of TEA-seq in other cell types will likely require sample-specific optimization.
source: It is likely that the use of TEA-seq in other cell types will require sample-specific optimization.
evidence: Based on speculation about future applications

claim: The requirement for neutrophil depletion may be limited to studies related to the immune system or immune-infiltrated tissues.
source: For example, the requirement for neutrophil depletion may be limited to studies related to the immune system or immune-infiltrated tissues.
evidence: Based on speculation about applicability to other tissues

claim: The value of debris and dead cell removal is likely to be applicable to disaggregated tissue samples from biopsies.
source: However, the value of debris and dead cell removal is likely to be applicable to disaggregated tissue samples from biopsies (Donlin et al., 2018).
evidence: Based on speculation with citation to Donlin et al., 2018

claim: High abundance of mononucleosomal fragments may indicate neutrophil-driven background in PBMCs.
source: In PBMCs, we found that high abundance of mononucleosomal fragments may indicate neutrophil-driven background, but this indicator of poor data quality may not be observed in other cell types or tissues.
evidence: Inferred from fragment length distribution data

claim: This indicator of poor data quality (high mononucleosomal fragments) may not be observed in other cell types or tissues.
source: In PBMCs, we found that high abundance of mononucleosomal fragments may indicate neutrophil-driven background, but this indicator of poor data quality may not be observed in other cell types or tissues.
evidence: Based on speculation about applicability to other cell types

claim: Low concentrations of digitonin were used to selectively permeabilize cholesterol-containing membranes while leaving the inner mitochondrial membrane intact.
source: Here, we have used low concentrations of digitonin to selectively permeabilize cholesterol-containing membranes, thereby leaving the inner mitochondrial membrane intact (Adam et al., 1990; Colbeau et al., 1971).
evidence: Supported by citations to Adam et al., 1990; Colbeau et al., 1971

claim: Different cell types have differing sensitivity to digitonin concentrations, perhaps reflecting natural variance in membrane cholesterol composition.
source: Different cell types have been shown to have differing sensitivity to digitonin concentrations, perhaps reflecting natural variance in membrane cholesterol composition (Holden and Horton, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Holden and Horton, 2009

claim: Cell permeabilization for TEA-seq may need to be optimized for other cell types.
source: As such, cell permeabilization for TEA-seq may need to be optimized for other cell types.
evidence: Based on speculation about future applications

claim: Optimization of cell permeabilization can be readily tested using bulk ATAC-seq and by measuring library complexity, FRIP score, and mitochondrial contamination.
source: This can be readily tested using bulk ATAC-seq and by measuring library complexity, FRIP score, and mitochondrial contamination to determine data quality.
evidence: Based on established methods for assessing ATAC-seq quality

claim: An online protocol for TEA-seq is maintained on the Protocols.io platform.
source: In addition to the Methods presented in this article, we are maintaining an online protocol to aid the research community in further development and adoption of TEA-seq on the Protocols.io platform (https://doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bqagmsbw).
evidence: Stated as fact

claim: Additional development could allow simultaneous measurement of additional aspects of cell biology.
source: Additional development could allow simultaneous measurement of additional aspects of cell biology (e.g., CpG sequencing methods, scCUT&Tag; Bartosovic et al., 2020), as well as improvements to the modalities in the TEA-seq trio (e.g., s3-ATAC, Mulqueen et al., 2021).
evidence: Based on speculation about future developments, with citations to Bartosovic et al., 2020; Mulqueen et al., 2021

claim: In direct comparisons of TEA-seq to existing methods, the sensitivity of gene detection was lower than CITE-seq.
source: In direct comparisons of TEA-seq to existing methods (CITE-seq and scATAC-seq), we found that the sensitivity of gene detection was lower and distributions of antibody detections were altered relative to CITE-seq; however, ATAC-seq data quality remained comparable to the standalone assay (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4

claim: Simultaneous, truly multimodal measurement across molecular compartments will be an essential tool to expand our view of the full picture of immune cell state in health and disease.
